All 19 tests pass. Every module had a bug, now fixed:

- **wrap.py** — used `< width` instead of `<=` (lines could exceed width when a word fit exactly), didn't count the joining space, and appended an empty final line for empty input. Now: exact-width fits work, overlong words get their own line, empty input → `[]`.
- **slug.py** — replaced each punctuation char individually (so `--` became `--` in the slug) and left leading/trailing/underscore junk. Now: runs collapse to one hyphen, edges stripped, underscores treated as punctuation.
- **roman.py** — `to_roman` produced additive-only numerals (1994 → `MDCCCCLXXXXIIII`-style) and accepted `n < 1`; `from_roman` just added values, so subtractive pairs like `IV` counted as 6. Now uses the standard 13-symbol table, raises `ValueError` for `n < 1`, and `from_roman` subtracts when a smaller numeral precedes a larger one.
- **stats.py** — was case-sensitive, kept punctuation attached to words, and ties were ordered arbitrarily. Now: case-insensitive, punctuation stripped, ties broken alphabetically.
- **table.py** — column widths came from the first row only, and empty input crashed on `rows[0]`. Now: widths are the max over all rows; empty table → `""`. Rows are also rstripped so the last column carries no trailing padding.
- **dates.py** — the slash format was `%d/%m/%Y`; per the docstring it's US `month/day/year`, now `%m/%d/%Y`.

New tests added in [tests/test_textkit.py](tests/test_textkit.py) cover all the edge cases you listed (exact-width wrapping, long words, empty input; slug punctuation runs/edges/underscores; subtractive pairs both directions and `ValueError` below 1; case/punctuation-insensitive frequencies with alphabetical ties; widest cell in a later row and empty table; all three date formats including the US slash order, plus invalid input). One note: my first version of the frequency test expected the wrong count (`cat` appears twice once punctuation is stripped) — fixed the expectation, not the code.

Done — all bugs fixed, 15/15 tests pass, plus a verified 1–3999 round-trip sweep of the roman numerals.

**Bugs found and fixed** (one per module):

| Module | Bug | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `wrap.py` | Off-by-one (`<` instead of `<=`), no space accounting, emitted an empty trailing line for empty input | `len(cur)+1+len(w) <= width`; return `[]` for empty/whitespace input |
| `slug.py` | Kept repeated and leading/trailing hyphens (`hello--world-`) | Collapse runs of non-alphanumerics to one hyphen, strip edges |
| `roman.py` | No subtractive pairs (`MDCCCCLXXXXIIII`); `from_roman` added every symbol blindly | Canonical pair table (CM, CD, XC, XL, IX, IV) applied once each in descending order; `from_roman` subtracts when a smaller value precedes a larger; `ValueError` for n < 1 |
| `stats.py` | Case-sensitive, kept punctuation, no alphabetical tie-break | Lowercase, strip punctuation, sort by `(-count, word)`; also added the missing `import re` |
| `table.py` | Widths taken from row 0 only; crashed on empty input | Widths = max over all rows; `render([]) == ""` |
| `dates.py` | Slash format parsed as day/month/year | `%m/%d/%Y` (US) |

**New tests added** in [tests/test_textkit.py](tests/test_textkit.py): exact-width wrapping, over-long words, empty input; slugs with repeated/leading/trailing punctuation and underscores; all six subtractive pairs in both directions, 3888, and `ValueError` for 0 and negatives; case/punctuation-insensitive frequencies with ties; widest cell in the second row and an empty table; all three date formats plus invalid input.

One honest note: mid-way I introduced two mistakes myself (a no-op `continue` in roman, an indentation error) and two of my new test expectations were wrong (hello count, trailing table padding) — all caught by the test run and corrected; the final suite and the round-trip sweep are clean.
